- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Versailles-Washington System refers to the political and economic order established in Europe after World War I.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Treaty of Versailles, signed in 1919, ended the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Treaty of Versailles imposed severe penalties and reparations on Germany.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Washington Naval Conference of 1921-1922 established a set of agreements on naval disarmament.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Washington Naval Conference aimed to prevent an arms race between major naval powers, including the United States, Britain, Japan, France, and Italy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Versailles-Washington system aimed to promote peace, stability, and international cooperation in the aftermath of World War I.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The system was based on the principles of collective security, as expressed in the League of Nations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The system also focused on the reduction of armaments to prevent future wars.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Versailles-Washington system ultimately failed to achieve its goals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The harsh terms imposed on Germany contributed to the rise of Nazi dictatorship.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Great Depression of the 1930s weakened the global economy and the political order established after World War I.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The failure of the Versailles-Washington system ultimately led to World War II.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] World War II marked the end of the Versailles-Washington system.
